title.narrative: Improving multi-hazard anticipatory action: economic shocks as a driver of need

description.narrative: This project seeks to strengthen resilience and reduce humanitarian need by improving multi -hazard anticipatory action through integrating economic shocks as a driver of humanitarian need. Result 1: A multi -hazard anticipatory action model that strongly embeds economic shocks as a key driver of humanitarian need. The main output of this project will be the integration of economic shocks in a multi -hazard anticipatory action model. The multi -hazard anticipatory action model will build on existing early warning systems and models for climate -induced shocks in Niger, but it will add an additional layer for economic shocks which will strengthen its relevance in contexts of economic instability. This requires further unpacking of ‘economic shocks' as a driver of humanitarian need in Niger. The action will draw on the experience, results and lessons learned from Oxfam and RECA, as well as from the interventions of the Ministry of Population, Social Action, and National Solidarity on disaster risk reduction and humanitarian responses. This project will consider and complement the experiences related to economic shocks, climate change and indigenous approaches to resilience of communities to significantly reduce vulnerability and poverty and mitigate the impact of crises. - Result 1.1 Relevant indicators and thresholds for economic shocks are identified. - Result 1.2 Indicators and thresholds for economic shocks are integrated in existing (climate -focused) AA frameworks. - Result 1.3 Appropriate anticipatory actions are mapped and identified. - Result 1.4 At -risk households can receive pre -emptive cash. Result 2: Building an evidence base and influencing of the humanitarian and development sectors. The project will build on close collaboration with relevant stakeholders at local, national, regional and global levels, including local government disaster management authorities, to ensure the sustainability of the project outcome.
